title: Optically Highlighting Basement Membrane Components in C. elegans
protocol: Mount transgenic worms of appropriate developmental stage into a 1.5 µl drop of M9 on a 5% noble agar pad with 0.01 M sodium azide atop a standard microscope slide.
Cover the worms with a standard glass coverslip.
Proceed to photoconversion using a 405 nm ultraviolet laser.
Use a laser scanning confocal microscope equipped with a 63X or 100X objective to acquire an image of the worm.
Photoconvert a region(s) of BM using a customizable ROI bleaching tool within the acquisition software.
Adjust the 405nm laser power to 1-2% and perform 100-200 iterations for optimal photoconversion.
Mark particular worms carefully if working with several worms per slide, especially on an inverted microscope by labeling under the slide opposite the coverslip.
Reduce the pinhole size on the confocal to minimize Dendra2 photoconversion above and below the focal plane.
Image worms immediately following photoconversion using a wide field fluorescence microscope or spinning disc confocal if appropriate for the experiment.
Use the same image acquisition settings if quantitative measurements are planned among different images.
Recover worms by sliding the coverslip back and picking with a glob of OP50 or using a mouth pipette and M9 to transfer animals to food plates.
Transfer worms to food (OP50 E. coli) plates for the necessary amount of time at the appropriate temperature as required by the experimental design.
Mount worms on new noble agar pad with 0.01M NaN3.
Use image analysis software to quantify changes in position or fluorescence intensities of regions of photoconverted BM in 3D over time.
Maintain consistent imaging acquisition settings between sessions or experiments.
